paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage hands you. Hezekiah had just been healed, and a visitor came with a gift. He showed that visitor EVERYTHING. When Isaiah asked what they had seen, he answered, "There is nothing among my treasures that I did not show them." (2 Kings 20:15). I think it's easy to pour the whole heart into what we own when life is going great.

Then comes the part that gets me. The LORD says through Isaiah that everything in the palace will be carried off to Babylon (2 Kings 20:17). Hezekiah answers, "The word of the LORD that you have spoken is good." For he thought, "Will there not at least be peace and security in my lifetime?" (2 Kings 20:19). I think he was looking at his own days and not at the family coming after him. Baker, I've been there. I once stared at my own cozy counter and never thought about who'd be sitting there after me.

So here's the big idea. Treasure doesn't last, but the word of the LORD does. Hezekiah's days of peace were a gift, and a gift like that is for sharing what the LORD has given, not for guarding what's in the storehouse. Ask yourself today what you're showing off and what you're passing on. The story isn't over, so keep your ovens ready and your eyes on what lasts.
